content:
Ambition Mechanical: LinkedIn Posts (Week of Mar 12)

Drafted by: Alex (Deal Architect) Date: 2026-03-12 Platform: LinkedIn (Ambition Mechanical business page) Status: DRAFT. Patrik approval required before posting.

Context

These 3 posts are designed to break 4+ weeks of silence on Ambition's LinkedIn. They're text-only, no video editing required. Ash or Patrik can copy-paste and post directly.

These are DIFFERENT from Tony's 6 drafts at projects/content-agent/output/ambition/first-linkedin-post-drafts.md. Tony's drafts are "first post" introductions. These 3 below are content posts that can run alongside or after Tony's opener. The recommended sequence:

  1. Thu Mar 13: Tony's Option A ("We've Been Here") as the inaugural post
  2. Fri Mar 14: One of these Alex posts below
  3. Mon Mar 17: Another Alex post below

This gives Ambition 3 posts in 5 days and breaks the silence with momentum.

Post 1: "The System Nobody Sees"

Best for: Showcasing HVAC expertise. Pairs well with any on-site photo.

Every building you walk into has a system keeping it comfortable. Rooftop units running in 115-degree heat. Piping threaded through ceilings. Controls calibrated so the temperature is right before anyone walks through the door.

That's what we do. 23 years of commercial HVAC, plumbing, and piping across Phoenix. Hospitals. Schools. Restaurants. Data centers. The kind of facilities where the system can't go down.

We just finished a complete mechanical install for a new commercial kitchen build in Scottsdale. Custom ductwork, grease exhaust, makeup air. Every line run clean, every connection tight.

If your building is running right, it's because somebody like us made sure it does.

ambitionmechanical.com

#CommercialHVAC #PhoenixContractor #MechanicalContractor #HVAC #ArizonaConstruction

Word count: 118 Content pillar: The Work Photo suggestion: Use one of the 25 real job site photos from the Ambition website. Din Tai Fung kitchen install or Primrose project photos would be ideal.

Post 2: "Phoenix Heat Is Not a Suggestion"

Best for: Local/seasonal angle. Phoenix-specific credibility. No photo needed (but one helps).

Phoenix summers don't negotiate. When it's 118 outside and your commercial HVAC goes down, every minute matters. Your employees can't work. Your customers leave. Your product spoils.

We've been handling emergency mechanical calls across the Valley for over two decades. Abraza. Primrose. INEOS. Facilities that call us because they know we pick up and we show up.

There's a reason companies keep our number saved. It's not marketing. It's 23 years of answering the phone when things break.

If your building needs mechanical work in the Phoenix heat, you want someone who's done this a few hundred times. That's us.

480-555-XXXX | ambitionmechanical.com

#PhoenixHVAC #EmergencyHVAC #CommercialMechanical #ArizonaBusiness #HVACContractor

Word count: 115 Content pillar: Local / Phoenix + Social Proof Photo suggestion: Any on-site crew photo or rooftop unit shot. Real photos only. The desert/heat angle works best with a visual of someone actually working in the heat. Note: Replace 480-555-XXXX with Ambition's real phone number before posting.

Post 3: "Before and After: What a Real Install Looks Like"

Best for: Transformation story. Visual impact. Strongest with a before/after photo pair.

People ask what commercial mechanical work actually looks like. Here's the short version:

Before: exposed structure, empty ceiling cavities, no climate system, raw space that can't be occupied.

After: full HVAC, plumbing, and piping running through every wall and ceiling. Temperature controlled. Water flowing. Exhaust vented. Building code passed. Doors open.

That transformation is what Ambition Mechanical does every day. We take commercial spaces from shell to fully operational. The work isn't glamorous, but without it, nothing else in the building works.

23 years. 500+ projects. Phoenix, Scottsdale, and across the Valley.

ambitionmechanical.com

#BeforeAndAfter #CommercialConstruction #HVAC #MechanicalContractor #PhoenixAZ #BuiltRight

Word count: 107 Content pillar: Before & After Photo suggestion: Before/after pair from any job site. The Primrose progress update footage or Din Tai Fung kitchen build would work. Even two stills from the same project at different stages. This post is 10x more effective with visuals.

Strategy Alignment

These posts align with the broader AOM strategy for Ambition:

  • Offer ladder: These aren't sales posts. They build credibility and visibility, which is the top of the funnel for a construction company. The CTA is soft: website link, phone number, "follow along." No hard sell.
  • Content pillars: All 3 map to the pillars defined in social-AGENT.md (The Work, Local/Phoenix, Before & After).
  • Brand voice: Confident, not cocky. Real work shown, not talked about. No corporate speak. Reads like a contractor who knows what they're doing, not a marketing agency.
  • Retainer justification: 3 posts this week + Tony's drafts = enough content for 2+ weeks of LinkedIn at 2/week. This buys time to get video editing flowing for Reels.
  • Upsell path: Consistent posting -> results -> justify rate increase from $2k to $3.5k/month. Can't raise the rate while delivering nothing.

What's Next

After these 3 posts + Tony's 3 drafts go live (6 total):

  1. Ambition has 2-3 weeks of LinkedIn covered
  2. Start weaving in video posts as Reels get edited (Cleo's briefs are ready)
  3. Message Mo with the proactive update (see ambition-content-emergency.md, Part 4)
  4. Build toward full delivery: 5 Reels/week + 2 LinkedIn/week by end of March

These posts are ready to copy-paste. Ash posts manually. No tools needed.
